raw_answer_text:
A1: The clk signal (all "p" pulses) toggles at a constant, regular rate throughout the diagram, unaffected by req/ack/done.
A2: All three signals — req, ack, and done — start low (0).
A3: The request signal transitions (asserts) first, rising before the acknowledge signal.
A4: No — in the waveform, ack only rises after req has already risen; there is no point where ack is high while req is still 0, so ack cannot assert before req.
A5: The diagram shows req falling only after ack has been high for several cycles, i.e., req returns low once acknowledge has asserted (the file does not state an explicit causal rule, only this timing order).
A6: The diagram shows ack falling only after req has already returned low, i.e., ack drops back to 0 once request has deasserted (again only the timing order is shown, not an explicit causal statement).
A7: The done signal goes high briefly (for two clock periods) right as req falls, marking completion of the handshake; it occurs after both req and ack have asserted, coinciding with req's return to low and just before ack itself falls.
A8: (1) req rises (0→1); (2) ack rises (0→1); (3) req falls (1→0), coinciding with done rising; (4) ack falls (1→0), after which done also falls.
